visa_requirement_type: Visa-exempt for Bangladesh; visitor permit may be granted at entry
maximum_permitted_stay: Up to 6 months on request; may be extended by the Chief Immigration Officer up to 12 months from entry.
passport_validity_rule: A valid passport is required. The Visa Exemption Order applies to persons holding a valid passport; the Act does not state a six-month minimum validity.
blank_passport_pages_rule: No minimum blank-page count specified in the cited Act.
return_ticket_rule: No universal return-ticket requirement is specified in the cited Act; an officer may assess the proposed visit and supporting travel arrangements.
proof_of_funds_rule: A person likely to become a public charge because of insufficient means may be inadmissible under the Act; no fixed minimum amount is published.
accommodation_rule: No universal hotel-booking or accommodation-document requirement is specified in the cited Act.
travel_insurance_rule: No mandatory visitor travel-insurance amount identified in the cited Act.
yellow_fever_or_health_rule: Vaccination certificate may be required for travellers arriving from countries designated endemic for cholera, plague or yellow fever; the regulations do not enumerate countries. Confirm with Montserrat Health/Immigration.
transit_rule: The cited Act and separate passport-exemption provisions do not establish a general Bangladesh-specific visa-free transit route. Confirm with Montserrat Immigration before relying on a transit exemption.
application_channel: No advance visa application is required for a Bangladesh ordinary passport holder because Bangladesh is expressly listed in the Immigration (Visa Exemption) Order. Present a valid passport at the port of entry and request a visitor permit from the Immigration Officer.
application_fee: No visa fee; visitor-permit fee not stated.
processing_time: No visa processing; permit decided at entry.
required_documents: Valid Bangladesh ordinary passport|Visitor permit requested from the Immigration Officer at the port of entry|Evidence of intended visit and onward arrangements if requested|Evidence of sufficient means if requested|Vaccination certificate if arriving from a country designated endemic for a listed disease|Health declaration or medical examination if directed
official_immigration_source_name: Government of Montserrat — Immigration Act, CAP 13.01 (2025 revision), including Immigration (Visa Exemption) Order and section 22
review_notes: The current official Immigration Act's Visa Exemption Order expressly lists Bangladesh. This is a visa exemption, not a visa on arrival. A valid passport remains required. Section 22 allows an Immigration Officer to grant a visitor permit for up to six months; the actual period is discretionary and recorded on the permit. The cited Act does not publish a complete Bangladesh-specific arrival checklist or a minimum passport-validity period. Invest Montserrat guidance is used only for general visitor preparation, not to override the statutory exemption.
notes: Bangladesh is explicitly included in the Immigration (Visa Exemption) Order. A visitor permit is not a visa on arrival: under section 22, an Immigration Officer may grant up to six months on request, and the Chief Immigration Officer may extend the permit up to twelve months from entry. Valid passport remains required. The Act permits officer-led photographs/fingerprints for a person to whom a permit is issued if required; no advance visa photo or size is prescribed.

visa_requirement_type: Visitor visa required; conditional exemption may apply with a valid UK, US or Canadian visa or residence permission
maximum_permitted_stay: The official visitor-visa page does not publish a fixed stay period; the period and conditions are set by the immigration authority at entry.
passport_validity_rule: Passport must have at least six months remaining before expiry; the official page phrases this as valid six months prior to expiration.
blank_passport_pages_rule: No minimum blank-page count specified in the cited visitor-visa guidance.
return_ticket_rule: The application form requests intended arrival and departure dates, but the public visa checklist does not state a universal return-ticket format.
proof_of_funds_rule: An original bank reference letter on behalf of the applicant is listed; no fixed minimum balance is published.
accommodation_rule: The application form asks for accommodation type and address; no universal hotel-booking format is published.
travel_insurance_rule: No mandatory travel-insurance amount or policy requirement is specified in the cited visitor-visa guidance.
yellow_fever_or_health_rule: No general tourist vaccination requirement was identified in the visitor-visa checklist reviewed. Follow any current public-health direction issued for the travel date.
transit_rule: No Bangladesh-specific transit-visa rule is stated on the public visitor-visa page; confirm with Border Force for airside or landside transit.
application_channel: Apply from outside the Islands through the nearest British High Commission, Embassy or Consulate, the Director of Immigration in Grand Turk, or the Turks and Caicos representatives in London or New York. The exact receiving mission for Bangladesh applications was not confirmed; contact Border Force before lodging.
application_fee: $100 admin fee + $150 on approval; currency not stated.
required_documents: Completed visitor visa application form|Passport meeting the published validity requirement|Two photographs certified by a Justice of the Peace|Current police record from country of origin|Employer letter or current business licence, as applicable|Original bank reference letter on behalf of applicant|Certified surety identification|Surety covering letter|Evidence of surety's legal status in the Turks and Caicos Islands|School letter and parents' status evidence where applicable
official_immigration_source_name: Government of the Turks and Caicos Islands — Visitor's Visa
review_notes: The official nationality-based visa-exemption list does not include Bangladesh, so an ordinary Bangladesh passport holder requires a visitor visa unless a separate conditional exemption applies. The official guidance says certain nationals not on the list may be granted entry without a TCI visa if they hold a valid visa or residence permission for the UK, United States or Canada; this is a conditional/discretionary exemption, not a general visa-free entitlement. The published fees are shown as '$' without a currency code; UniGo does not infer USD. The exact Bangladesh receiving mission and processing time are not stated on the official page.
notes: The official linked application form is dated 2016 and the Border Force entry page was checked on 2026-11-15. Confirm current fee currency, receiving mission, and any updated checklist with TCI Border Force before payment or travel. Bangladesh is absent from the current visa-exempt nationality list reviewed. Conditional UK/US/Canada visa or residence exemptions may apply only under the published terms.

visa_requirement_type: Australian Visitor visa (subclass 600) Tourist stream required for entry from outside Australia; no separate Cocos visa
maximum_permitted_stay: Generally 3 months; up to 12 months may be granted in certain circumstances. The visa grant specifies the actual stay period.
passport_validity_rule: A valid passport or travel document is required. The overseas Tourist stream page does not state a universal six-month minimum validity.
blank_passport_pages_rule: No minimum blank-page count specified on the subclass 600 Tourist stream page.
return_ticket_rule: No universal pre-purchased return-ticket rule is stated on the route page; evidence of travel plans and ability to leave Australia may be requested.
proof_of_funds_rule: Applicants must have enough money for the stay and to leave Australia; no fixed minimum balance is published.
accommodation_rule: Include accommodation and travel plans where relevant; no single mandatory booking format is published.
travel_insurance_rule: No mandatory visitor insurance amount is stated on the Tourist stream page. Home Affairs strongly recommends adequate health insurance because visitors may be liable for healthcare costs.
yellow_fever_or_health_rule: Home Affairs may request health examinations or other checks depending on the case. The Cocos travel page says special vaccinations are not required for travel to the Islands.
transit_rule: If travelling from mainland Australia to Cocos, passports and visas are not required for the domestic leg. If entering from outside Australia, normal Australian Customs and Immigration procedures apply. Australian transit-visa rules may apply to a separate transit itinerary.
application_channel: Apply online through ImmiAccount for the Visitor visa subclass 600 Tourist stream while outside Australia and remain outside Australia until the decision. Home Affairs may request biometrics at an Australian biometric collection centre in Bangladesh.
application_fee: See Home Affairs Visa Pricing Estimator; static page omits amount.
processing_time: Check Home Affairs processing-time guide; indicative, not guaranteed.
required_documents: Valid passport and identity documents|Evidence of travel plans and intended activities|Evidence of sufficient funds for stay and departure|Evidence of genuine temporary visit and reasons to return to Bangladesh|Accommodation details or host invitation where relevant|Employment, business, study or retirement evidence relevant to the applicant|English translations for documents not in English
official_immigration_source_name: Australian Government Department of Infrastructure — Cocos (Keeling) Islands travel information
review_notes: The Australian Government's official Cocos travel page states that passports and visas are not required for travel from mainland Australia, but normal Australian Customs and Immigration procedures apply when entering from outside Australia. Bangladesh ordinary passport holders are not in the eligible passport classes for ETA subclass 601 or eVisitor subclass 651, so the appropriate tourism route is the Visitor visa subclass 600 Tourist stream, applied for online through ImmiAccount. The visa is electronically linked to the passport. The grant determines the actual stay and entries.
notes: This is a territory entry record, not a separate visa regime. A Bangladesh traveller already admitted to mainland Australia may travel to Cocos as a domestic leg without a separate territory visa; direct arrival from outside Australia requires the normal Australian visa. The Cocos page states no special vaccinations are required and advises checking health insurance because serious cases may be referred to Perth.

visa_requirement_type: U.S. B-2 or combined B1/B2 visitor visa required; U.S. immigration law applies to Puerto Rico
maximum_permitted_stay: The period of admission is determined by U.S. Customs and Border Protection at entry. Visa validity is not the permitted stay period.
passport_validity_rule: Passport must generally be valid at least six months beyond the intended period of stay unless a country-specific agreement exempts the traveller; no Bangladesh exemption was identified in the guidance reviewed.
blank_passport_pages_rule: No fixed blank-page count stated on the general visitor-visa page.
return_ticket_rule: No universal pre-purchased return-ticket requirement is stated; the applicant must establish intent to depart after the temporary visit.
proof_of_funds_rule: Applicant must show ability to pay all trip costs; no fixed minimum bank balance is published.
accommodation_rule: No universal hotel booking requirement is stated; itinerary and accommodation details may support the purpose of travel.
travel_insurance_rule: No mandatory visitor travel-insurance requirement is stated on the cited visitor-visa guidance.
yellow_fever_or_health_rule: No special visa-related vaccination rule is stated on the cited visitor-visa page; check current CDC and port-of-entry requirements.
transit_rule: A C-1 transit visa may be required for immediate and continuous transit unless the traveller already holds a visa or exemption permitting transit; a valid B1/B2 visa may be used for transit. Check the official transit-visa guidance for the itinerary.
application_channel: Complete DS-160 online, pay the nonimmigrant visa application fee and schedule an interview through the current U.S. Embassy Dhaka appointment system. The U.S. Department of State's wait-time table lists Dhaka for B1/B2 interviews. Follow local post instructions.
application_fee: US$185 MRV fee; no B1/B2 issuance fee.
processing_time: Dhaka B1/B2 wait (21 Oct 2026): 8.5-month average; 1.5-month next slot. Not decision time.
required_documents: Valid passport|DS-160 confirmation page|MRV fee payment receipt where required before interview|Digital photo uploaded through DS-160; one printed photo only if upload fails or the post requests it|Evidence of trip purpose|Evidence of intent to depart after the visit|Evidence of ability to pay all trip costs|Employment, business, study or family-tie evidence relevant to the applicant
official_immigration_source_name: U.S. Department of State — Visitor Visa (B-2 or combined B1/B2)
review_notes: The Immigration and Nationality Act defines the United States geographically to include Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. The Department of State requires a B-2 or combined B1/B2 visitor visa for foreign nationals travelling to the United States for tourism unless they qualify for the Visa Waiver Program; Bangladesh is not a VWP participating nationality. The Bangladesh reciprocity schedule specifies B1/B2 as one entry with 3 months validity and no issuance fee. The MRV application fee is US$185. CBP determines the actual period of admission.
notes: Puerto Rico is a U.S. territory for immigration-law purposes, not a separate visa jurisdiction. The Bangladesh B1/B2 reciprocity period is one entry/3 months validity; it does not authorise a three-month stay automatically. The U.S. Department of State's Dhaka B1/B2 interview-wait figures are updated monthly and are not adjudication guarantees. The accessible Dhaka post guidance did not confirm an additional printed-photo requirement when DS-160 upload succeeds; bring one printed photo if upload fails or local instructions require it.
